quoted.text:
A trader who’s compounded at 60% a year with a Sortino over 2 on why he refuses to compete with the pods on their timeframe:

Joe Walsh is the Founding Partner of hedge fund Code Partners.

Joe Walsh explains:

“The first thing I think about is time horizon.”

“I don’t want to be valuing a security on a three to six month timeframe where I’m competing against a very well-resourced, motivated person inside one of these firms with way better corporate access, way better short-term information, proprietary data sets.”

“You’ve got to pick your time horizons to be avoiding very good players. You’ve got to pick your sectors where all the pods who used to do that have been shut down and all the investors have given up.”

“The game selection aspect is running away from competition, and that’s where greater inefficiency by definition lives. There are huge pockets of that in the equity market today.”

“If you think you’re going to have a huge edge trading European industrials on a three-month timeframe, I would politely disagree.”

“We have huge edge in timeframes greater than 12 months, in sectors and markets that are just not as competitive. It’s not worth their time, when they’re running $100 billion levered multiple times, to muck around in names with $10, 20, 30 million a day of liquidity.”

“The capacity I could run money with is very attractive, to single digit billions, and still have a huge edge and still remain very liquid.”

Kraken co-CEO Arjun Sethi says unlike banks, he doesn't want to pocket the interest margin, and wants to give most of that yield back to customers

"As we're moving more into our own rails and infrastructure, we have to innovate and actually disrupt some of our existing products and make it where we make less money or we don't make money."

"When you think about fees or intermediaries or even things that we charge for over time, we have to be able to continue to bring that down or move on with a new business model, because someone else will actually go out and say, I don't want to rent-seek this."

"I think that ends up becoming a really important piece of any of these traditional institutions, which is how are they going to innovate moving forward?"

"The one thing we continue to hear is you need to be able to be a bank to be able to offer yield. Well, I'm not interested in the net interest margin for ourselves."

"In some cases, it'll be good for us. But in many cases, imagine bringing all that interest margin back to our customers. It's their yield."

"I just think that's just such a core piece of what you want to be able to do on behalf of your customers."

The question is not if we will have a bear market, the question is if this administration can afford to let us have a bear market. 

- AI Capex is 50% of GDP. If it stops or slows down, GDP growth goes down the drain. No GDP growth = recession. Mainstreet gets hit the worst as the labor market will collapse. 

- 90% of consumer spending is done by the top 10%. They are levered against their assets that allow them to keep spending because their stocks keep going up. Stocks go down? Goodbye to consumer spending as we enter an actual recession given normal consumers already are borrowing from credit cards to pay for everything. 

- Social security will be wrecked over the coming 10 years. Why do you think we got the Trump Accounts? Because the administration believes in financial literacy? No, they need a replacement and having kids compound in the stock market to basically build their retirement account from birth could replace social security. That means stocks have to go up for those accounts to be worth anything and actually compound. Most 401Ks in this country are basically seen as retirement accounts. If the admin lets the market crash, people will not be able to afford retirement when social security benefits get cut into 2032. 

- We are $40T in debt. Bond yields continue to go higher which means the interest expense on our debt is approaching a significant part of our overall spending. The literal only way to solve this is cut spending or grow. Repubs or Dems will not cut spending…so growth is the only answer. If the market crashes, the chances of sustained growth in the greatest tech buildout we have ever seen will be impossible and ultimately make our debt situation even worse. We have to grow.

Not saying we can’t get into some horrible bear market, but given how levered the entire economy is to AI, which is basically the entire stock market, I do think this admin will try very hard to make sure we don’t have some horrible, ugly crash. If they let it happen, everything goes down the drain and the difference between now and dotcom is that demand for GPUs is very real (no oversupply) and the difference between now and 2008 is that the potential credit issue is not in housing and banks, it’s within GPUs and there is so much demand that the hyperscalers + Nvidia + the admin could come in to make sure things don’t get as bad as then. 

Maybe we could have some epic crash, but this administration really cannot afford to let that happen.

Token2049 期间，我受邀参加了火币的内部活动，做了一场 panel 分享，也出席了他们的 VIP 晚宴。另外和孙宇晨孙哥@justinsuntron 即兴约了一场采访，目前正在打磨问题。

**先替火币澄清一件事。晚宴原定 6 号，后来因为安排调整改到了 8 号。工作人员是真的尽心尽力，我亲眼看着他们为了协调好每一个人，焦灼地忙了全程。办过活动的人都知道，现场总有太多突发状况：场地临时变更，容纳人数跟着变，这些未知因素导致一些 VIP 没能到场。但团队自始至终都在积极解决问题。

火币的现场活动给我一种很不一样的感觉。在其他交易所的夹击之下，来到现场的反而都是火币多年的老用户，整场氛围其乐融融，非常家人向🙏感谢 @Ceee333_ 的邀请，她是这场活动的负责人之一，也是双语主持，业务能力相当过硬。还有@HTX_Molly @Lumibb_ @Xiaodu_HTX 等火币的小伙伴，每个人都很 energetic。这是我第一次深度接触火币的活动对接团队，评价很高（我不是托，是托死全家）。

**再说说我筹划的这场采访（目前身体太差的确稍微拖延了）。我有稍微看了下孙哥和邵艾伦那场”薄肌”采访，以及和自由潜冠军金明聊 Crypto、AI 与量子威胁的那场。我想问点不太一样的人文向问题，因为我的视角可能有些特别：我是从新概念时期就知道孙哥的。同为新概念作文大赛的获奖者，他某种程度上算是我的前辈。我第一次听到这个名字，是在《萌芽》上读到他写的《一道论证题》，所以对他的文青之路一路追踪非常熟稔。

我也注意到，孙哥提到他们生态里一直比较活跃的以太坊挖矿活动，所以也想专门问问他怎么看 ETH 这个资产。对于BTC被攻破这块，我和以太坊基金会做抗量子研究和在Yale/MIT读相关PHD的一些朋友交流过，他们对 Q-Day 的到来目前还算比较乐观，这个话题也想和他聊聊。

**最后一个小提议：**除了数学奖，火币很值得再设一个文学奖/人文奖。我感觉现在这些交易所办的这种访谈活动，基本上都是跟交易员对谈，来来回回，其实也都是那些交易员，同质化程度太高了，包括打广告的 KOL 也是，基本上是今天做完交易所 A 的广告，明天又去发交易所 B 的广告。孙哥既是新概念出身，又做过社交 App（陪我），某种程度上“薄肌”也算是一种文化输出了，那是否火币可以系统性以活动的形式支持更多元的加密文化输出？

先发散到这儿，抛砖引玉，之后再细聊。

To fill 600 liter tanks at 600 bars (8700 PSI) takes, in theory, 220 MJoules. 

Taking into account the efficiency of the complex compressor requires for this, the total energy consumed would probably be around 400MJ, or about 110 kWh (more energy than a full Tesla S battery).

This would take at least 12 hours with current compressor technology (which requires dessication, cooling, etc).

All of this for a few seconds of jet boost.
